memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The angel of the LORD said to Balaam, "Go with the men, but speak only what I tell you." So Balaam went with Balak's officials. When Balak heard that Balaam was coming, he went out to meet him at the Moabite town on the Arnon border, at the edge of his territory. - Num 22:35-36 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Balaam is permitted to continue, but under a firm condition: he must speak only what God tells him. The proud prophet who set out to earn a reward is now on a very short leash. He may go, but he is no longer in control of his own tongue. God will govern every word.

Meanwhile Balak, eager and expectant, rushes out to meet Balaam at the edge of his territory. He believes he is about to secure the curse he has paid for. Neither man yet realises that God has already determined the outcome. The whole scheme is under the Lord's sovereign hand.

Here is a truth that steadies the soul. Even the plans of those who oppose God's people are ultimately subject to God's control. Balaam could not curse where God intended to bless. Balak's silver could not buy what God had forbidden. The Lord was quietly overruling everything for the good of His people.

This is our confidence in Christ. No scheme against God's children can succeed beyond what He permits, and He works even the plots of enemies for good (Rom 8:28). When you feel powers arrayed against you, remember that they too are on God's leash. Nothing touches you outside His sovereign, loving purpose.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you trust that even opposition is under God's sovereign control?
2. How does God's rule over Balaam's tongue comfort you today?
3. Where do you need to rest in God's power over the schemes around you?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Sovereign Lord, thank You that even those who oppose Your people are under Your control. When schemes surround me, help me rest in Your power to work all things for good. Amen.
